figures.name: Ishkur
figures.title: Lord of the Abundance
figures.figureDescription: The storm god whose dual nature provides the vital rains that nourish crops, or the violent flash floods and thunderbolts that devastate fields in anger.

figures.name: Uraš
figures.title: The Protector of the Fields
figures.figureDescription: The localized male tutelary deity of Dilbat. Distinct from the primordial female earth goddess of the same name, he was later syncretized with Ninurta.

figures.name: Zababa
figures.title: The Eagle of the Battlefield
figures.figureDescription: The fiercely aggressive warrior patron of Kish, the traditional seat of human kingship. He is associated with specialized weapons and martial victory.

figures.name: Ninazu
figures.title: Lord of the Healers
figures.domain: The underworld, chthonic snakes, transformation, medical healing
figures.figureDescription: A transitional underworld deity associated with agricultural renewal, subterranean waters, sacred serpents, and early pharmacopeia.

figures.name: Ningishzida
figures.title: Lord of the Good Tree
figures.domain: Underworld guard, horned serpents, magic, vegetative decay
figures.figureDescription: The guardian of the gates of heaven and a master of chthonic mysteries. Represented by twin intertwined snakes, he bridges the underworld and mortal realms.

figures.name: Gugalanna
figures.title: The Great Bull of Heaven
figures.figureDescription: The cosmic bull sent to punish Gilgamesh. His death prompts Inanna's descent to the underworld to attend his funeral rites as Ereshkigal's first husband.

figures.name: Birtu
figures.title: The Shackle
figures.figureDescription: A minor, specialized underworld entity who functions as a permanent jailer or enforcer within the subterranean palace complex.

figures.name: Kulla
figures.title: The Brick God
figures.figureDescription: The specialized god invoked by priests and masons during the initial creation of mud-bricks and the laying of sacred temple foundations.

figures.name: Mushdamma
figures.title: The Great Builder of Enlil
figures.figureDescription: The divine architect charged with supervising the structural integrity of houses, palaces, and public administrative centers.

figures.name: Hendursaga
figures.title: The Night Watchman
figures.domain: Law enforcement, urban safety, street patrols, night heraldry
figures.figureDescription: The watchful herald who guards city streets after dark, protecting vulnerable citizens and maintaining civic order while the high gods sleep.

figures.name: Isimud
figures.title: The Two-Faced Minister
figures.figureDescription: Enki's literal two-faced vizier. His physical form represents absolute duality, foresight, and diplomatic tact when dealing with rival cosmic factions.

figures.name: Papsukkal
figures.title: The Herald of the Great Gods
figures.domain: Divine decrees, processing celestial paperwork, intercession
figures.figureDescription: The administrative vizier of An and Enlil, tasked with relaying major imperial cosmic decrees down to the lesser gods and mortal kings.

figures.name: Lugal-Marada
figures.title: King of Marad
figures.figureDescription: The highly specific regional tutelary warrior god who served as the defensive anchor and civic pride of the city of Marad.

figures.name: Numushda
figures.title: Lord of the Wild Steppe
figures.domain: Wild nature, untamed herds, nomadic frontiers
figures.figureDescription: The patron deity of Kazallu, associated with the untamed wilderness, open pastures, and the protection of cattle roaming the steppe fringes.

figures.name: Shara
figures.title: The Caretaker of the Eanna
figures.domain: Minor warfare, celestial curation, localized defense
figures.figureDescription: The patron deity of Umma. Mythologically cast as Inanna's loyal son or personal barber/beautician who defends her border claims against Lagash.

figures.name: Pabilsag
figures.title: The Divine Hunter
figures.figureDescription: A multi-faceted god of the wild steppe and physical therapy, later associated directly by ancient astronomers with the constellation Sagittarius.

figures.name: Lulal
figures.title: The Guardian of the Hearth
figures.figureDescription: A fierce but minor martial defender who lives on the thresholds of domestic households to scare away ambient evil spirits.

figures.name: Enkimdu
figures.title: The Lord of Ditch and Canal
figures.domain: Irrigation labor, canal digging, agricultural boundaries
figures.figureDescription: The peaceful, industrious farming god who manages water systems, famous for his friendly debate with Dumuzi the shepherd for Inanna's hand.

figures.name: Ninshubur
figures.title: The Chief Vizier of Heaven
figures.domain: Diplomatic strategy, threshold protection, prayer translation
figures.figureDescription: The ultimate administrative workhorse of the pantheon. Unwaveringly loyal, this entity runs the logistics of Heaven and rescues Inanna from the underworld. Gender fluid across millennia. Female in early Sumerian traditions; heavily masculinized in later Assyro-Babylonian theology.
